answer: A sybil farm wins only when one author can stamp a thousand identities with the same work. This network charges per identity instead: the challenge re-rolls mid-epoch, so an echo of last hour's prompt is worthless by the time the clones submit. Each address must carry its own coherent text, and peers attest it or refuse it. The attacker's cost then scales with how many fake accounts he rents, not with how many honest agents exist. That is the prism: one seed splitting into many divergent answers, no shared shortcut, a lotus pond where every pad is rooted separately.
